findings.claim: A same-named project copy is two definitions of one persona sharing one memory folder. The agent name is the exact-match key: dispatch uses it, the host resolves it, and the persona's memory lives at .claude/agent-memory/<name>/. The spec lets two writers mint that name, the shipped file and a forked copy. The copy carries a stale voice, gates and calibration, yet it reads and writes the same memory folder, and its replies feed the same validator. Understanding records written by the old persona are consumed by the forked one, and the reverse. FR-001 keeps chorus out of run settings, but the memory folder is persona identity, not a run setting, and the accepted cost names only the voice. Remedy: add one line to the FR-004 cost statement saying the copy shares the persona's memory folder, so after a plugin update the reader re-compares both the file and the folder. Default reading: one reviewer, one memory; offer changing the copy's memory scope as the alternative.

evidence.note: Dispatch and memory recovery are keyed by persona name, so a same-named copy is read as the same persona.
The agent-memory layout is .claude/agent-memory/<persona-name>/, keyed by name.

evidence.ref: Ubiquitous Language: an exact-match key with two writers returns plausible wrong answers, not errors
evidence.note: Two definitions behind one key never raise an error.

findings.pull_quote: The copy shares the original's memory, so a stale persona quietly reads and writes the live one's records.
findings.need_info_reason: I have not checked how Claude Code scopes 'memory: project' when a project-level file shadows a plugin file of the same name.

findings.claim: The spec's vocabulary drifts across reviewer, persona, lens and agent file. The title and FR-003 say 'reviewer', the Edge Cases say 'persona', and the canon says persona and lens. Only 'Project-level agent file' is defined in Key Entities; 'reviewer' is never tied to 'persona'. The README reader is a newcomer. Remedy: use 'reviewer' in the README, define it once as 'a chorus persona, one agent file', and add that clause to Key Entities.

evidence.note: The canon speaks of persona and lens, not reviewer.
The spec switches between 'reviewer' and 'persona' within one edge case.

findings.pull_quote: One word should name the thing a person retunes, and the README should define it once.

findings.claim: The rule sits in the right place, but the record cannot name a retuned reviewer. Persona files are supporting subdomain, and FR-001 keeps run settings out of the Core (the conductor), which is correct. The cost: a vote from a forked persona is indistinguishable in the record from one by the shipped persona, so the record's language claims a persona voted when a variant did. I do not re-argue the ruling. Remedy: keep the Out-of-scope entry, and add one sentence to the README cost statement that a round's record does not say which reviewers ran from a project copy.

evidence.note: Core is the conductor's procedure and invariants; personas are supporting.
Record visibility is declared out of scope.

findings.pull_quote: The record will say 'Beck voted' when a modified Beck did.
